# MotionSpec — web animation accessibility MCP server and CLI

> MotionSpec (npm: motionspec; GitHub: MasterPlayspots/motionspec) compiles validated animation specs to deterministic GSAP + CSS and statically checks loaded CSS for motion-accessibility candidates. It is not the Android/iOS MotionSpec class, Motion.dev / Framer Motion, a calendar app, or a video generator.

- Start: https://motionspec.dev/docs · repo: https://github.com/MasterPlayspots/motionspec
- Install: https://github.com/MasterPlayspots/motionspec/blob/main/llms-install.md
- Motion accessibility and audit limits: https://github.com/MasterPlayspots/motionspec/blob/main/docs/motion-accessibility.md
- MCP identity: io.github.MasterPlayspots/motionspec · npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/motionspec
- Hosted MCP: https://api.motionspec.dev/mcp (Streamable HTTP). Keyless: motion_catalog and motion_validate. Hosted motion_compile, motion_audit and motion_stats require a key.
- Local MCP: npx -y motionspec (stdio); all five tools, no key. Local CLI executable: motion. There is no standalone CLI validate command; compile validates first.
- Workflow: motion_catalog → write a spec → motion_validate → review warnings even when ok=true → motion_compile. URL checks use motion_audit, not motion_validate.
- Compiler: vanilla-gsap is the only public output target. Reduced-motion guards and loop pause controls are defaults; explicit opt-outs produce warnings. Internal WAAPI lowering is not a released CLI/MCP target.
- Scope: WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide, A) and 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) motion candidates; prefers-reduced-motion, CSS animation and pause paths. Static signals do not prove WCAG conformance. Runtime JS/GSAP, flashing, video and Canvas are not audited. The legacy reduced-motion-safe badge means zero findings in loaded CSS only.
- Agent rules: https://github.com/MasterPlayspots/motionspec/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- Contact: hello@motionspec.dev
